chunks: It was narrated to me from ʿAbd Allah — meaning Ibn al-Mughirah — raising it to Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام that the kurr is six hundred ratls. 6- And this report was narrated by Muhammad ibn ʿAli ibn Mahbub, from al-ʿAbbas, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu ʿAbd Allah عليه السلام.

He said: I said to him: A pond has collected water in it; beasts urinate in it, dogs lap from it, and the person in janabah performs ghusl in it. He said: If it is the measure of a kurr, nothing makes it najis, and the kurr is six hundred ratls.

The manner of preferring this report in considering the Iraqi ratls is that what is intended by it is the ratl of Makkah, because it equals two ratls. And it is not impossible that they عليهم السلام gave the questioner a fatwa according to the customary measure of his land, because it is not permissible that what is intended by it be the ratls of the people of Iraq nor the ratls of the people of al-Madinah, since none of our companions considered that, so it is abandoned by consensus. As for the preference of the one who considered the ratls of the people of al-Madinah by saying that precaution requires it, because if we carry it upon the greater measure the lesser enters into it, this is unsound, because one may say that this is contrary to precaution, since it is required of a person that he not perform the salat except by making wudu with water when it exists, and that he not judge a present water to be najis except with a legal proof. There is no disagreement among our companions that if water is less than the amount that we considered, then it becomes najis by what falls into it; and there is no proof here that if it exceeds what we considered, then it becomes najis by what falls into it. As for what was preferred on the basis of their custom, inasmuch as they were from the people of al-Madinah عليهم السلام, there is no preference in that, because they used to give fatwa according to what was customary in the questioner’s practice and usage. For that reason, in considering the ratls of the saʿ we regarded it as nine ratls in the Iraqi measure, and that is contrary to their own custom. Likewise, the report about which we have spoken, regarding their consideration of six hundred ratls, is only a consideration according to the custom of the people of Makkah. Thus they عليهم السلام used to take into account the custom of the other lands according to what they were asked about.

key_terms.الِاحْتِيَاطُ: juristic precaution in determining legal application
key_terms.الْإِجْمَاعِ: consensus of the Shia scholars or companions
key_terms.الْغَدِيرُ: a pond or pool of collected water
key_terms.الْكُرُّ: the legal quantity of water that is not rendered najis by impurity
key_terms.رِطْلٍ: a unit of weight or measure used to quantify the kurr
key_terms.عَادَةِ: customary local usage or convention in measurement
key_terms.نَجَاسَةِ: ritual impurity affecting the legal status of water
key_terms.يُنَجِّسْهُ: renders it najis or causes ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: What is the measure of kurr water in this hadith, and how are the six hundred ratls understood?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal measure of kurr water and states that water reaching the amount of a kurr is not rendered najis by impurities falling into it. The accompanying discussion examines how the measure of six hundred ratls should be understood, arguing that it refers to the Makkan standard in accordance with the questioner’s customary usage.
